Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Opportunities in Renewable
Energy Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s
(MSCI S&C’s) outputs are determined. Opportunities in Renewable Energy is a Key Issue in the
Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their positioning to
meet market demand for renewable power through capacity additions and network expansion.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

Opportunities associated with this Key Issue
• Increased revenues from utilizing public subsidies.
• Increased revenue due to changing consumer demand.
• Increased access to markets due to renewable power generation mandates (state, national or
regional objectives).
• Increased market share in specific market segments due to early-mover status.

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Opportunities in Renewable Energy Strategy score
The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Strategy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to expand
renewable energy capacity through strategic investments, internal structures, and quantitative targets. It
is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Targets to increase renewable capacity
Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed quantitative targets to increase renewable
energy capacity. Includes targets referring to owned capacity only, i.e., excluding purchasing
agreements. Applies to companies with an electricity generation business only.

• Internal structures to develop renewable capacity
Definition: Assesses the company’s established internal structures related to developing renewable
capacity. Best practice is to have a dedicated renewable energy subsidiary or be wholly involved in
renewables. Applies to companies with an electricity generation business only.
• Investments to increase connection of renewable power to electric grid
Definition: Indicates whether the company has made investments related to the increased connection of
renewable power to the electric grid. Applies to companies with an electricity transmission or distribution
business only.
• Score of planned additional renewable electricity generation relative to current total
capacity
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on ratio of planned additional renewable electricity
generation to current total capacity. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of
performance.
o Current Total Installed Capacity (MW)
Definition: The current amount of installed capacity for power generation in megawatts (MW).
o Additional renewable capacity (MW)
Definition: The amount of capacity in megawatts (MW) that an issuer has disclosed as planned additions
which are renewables.
Opportunities in Renewable Energy Programs & Initiatives score
The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Programs & Initiatives score evaluates the company’s initiatives
to expand renewable energy opportunities through customer green power options and
commercialization of renewable power equipment. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates
strong initiatives.
• Commercializes renewable power equipment
Definition: Indicates whether the company implements programs that involve the installation of
equipment used in renewable energy generation.
• Offers customers a green power option

Definition: Indicates whether the company offers its customers the option to purchase power from
renewable generation sources. Applies to companies with an electricity supply business only.
Opportunities in Renewable Energy Performance score
The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Performance score evaluates the company’s performance on
opportunities in renewable energy metrics (including renewable capacity and percentage change in the
proportion of renewable capacity to total generation capacity) relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0-
10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.
• Renewable power capacity performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on total renewable energy power capacity (as a
percentage of total installed capacity), and trend in renewable energy power capacity, relative to its
peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.
o Renewable power capacity (% of total installed capacity) score
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on installed renewable power capacity
expressed (as a percentage of total installed capacity). Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10
indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average renewable power capacity (% of total installed capacity)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average installed renewable capacity (as
a percentage of total installed capacity).
o Renewable power capacity (% of total installed capacity) industry relative trend score
Definition: Assesses the company’s three-year average of year-over-year installed
renewable power capacity (as a percentage of total installed capacity) trend, relative to its
peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
 Three-year average renewable power capacity trend (% of total installed
capacity)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year installed
renewable capacity (as a percentage of total installed capacity) trend.

Business Segment Exposure scores
The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business
segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the
Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define
business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business
Segment Exposure score. The Business Segment Exposure score is determined by a qualitative
assessment of whether a business activity has a core involvement in power generation. A higher
involvement will result in a higher exposure score for the business activity.

The following types of regulatory, fiscal and public financing incentives are considered for the Total
Incentives score:
1. Feed-in tariffs
2. Tradable energy certificates
3. Renewable portfolio standards
4. Capital subsidies, grants or rebates
5. Investment tax credits
6. Sales tax credits
7. Tax exemptions/reductions
8. Public investment loans
9. Public competitive bidding
The Total Incentives score measures the number of incentives provided by a country. Provision of more
incentives results in a higher opportunity score for a country or market.
The Renewable Energy Outlook for a country or market is based on a qualitative assessment by MSCI on
the planned renewable capacity additions and investments in renewable power generation in the country
or market.
